items.title: Ferrand Clementin Interview, 1973-08-02
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'storm, Betsy' as a weather event/hurricane, not a person.

ctx.x: Yeah, that was the worst storm. But those come late, they speak worst. Like, yeah. How do you call the one that? Betsy. Betsy. Betsy. Betsy. Betsy. Betsy's dog. And the head kind of one? Where you got to treat you with that storm?

Well, that used to storm. But that was the only one that ever. At that time, it was 1915. It didn't do much damage. It done a lot of damage. It didn't go down there. Everything you could hit. Mostly. But this storm, Betsy, there was so many people, so many houses. It was so big like this. There wasn't no more wind. It didn't blow no more water than it did in 1915.
There was a lot of water down there. Oh, yeah. There they had water.
